title: USB 2.0 spec (usb_20.pdf) -- chirp/reset speed-negotiation FSM, PING flow control, and the 4 transfer-type semantic rules
summary: Deep extraction of D:\DV\Task\USB\DOC\usb_20.pdf (Universal Serial Bus Spec Rev 2.0), citations by pdftotext -layout line number in .work\pdftxt\usb20.txt (32813 lines). CHIRP/RESET FSM (sec 7.1.7.5, spec p.153-154, lines 8622-8721): hub asserts SE0 at time T0 -> device (per prior state: suspend/FS/HS, three sub-cases with distinct wait windows TFILTSE0/TWTRSTFS/TWTREV+TWTRSTHS) drives Chirp K for >=1.0ms and <=7.0ms after T0 (TUCH/TUCHEND) -> hub detects Chirp K after >=2.5us (TFILT), else continues SE0 to end of reset (fallback to FS/LS) -> within <=100us of chirp-K ending (TWTDCH) hub emits alternating Chirp K/J with no idle gaps until 100-500us before end of Reset (TDCHSE0), each chirp 40-60us (TDCHBIT) -> device must detect the 6-symbol sequence Chirp K-J-K-J-K-J (each >=2.5us TFILT) -> on success, within <=500us (TWTHS) device drops D+ pullup, enables HS terminations, enters HS Default; on failure within 1.0-2.5ms (TWTFS) device reverts to FS Default. Overall reset duration: hub-port >=10ms (TDRST), root-port >=50ms (TDRSTR, gaps between bursts <3ms TRHRSI), reset recovery time 10ms (TRSTRCY) before hub/device must accept new commands. Chirp DC levels: Chirp J = D+-D- >=+300mV at target connector, Chirp K <=-300mV (line 8358-8366). Note line 8654-5: because downstream port isn't in Transmit state during Reset Protocol, HS chirp levels must not provoke disconnect detection -- relevant to disconnect-checker false-positive avoidance. PING FLOW CONTROL (sec 8.5.1, p.217, lines 11856-11910): HS control-OUT (data/status stages only, NOT setup stage) and HS bulk-OUT endpoints must support PING. Host sends PING token -> device NAK (no space for wMaxPacketSize payload, host may retry later, not grounds to retire transfer) or ACK (space available, host must issue actual OUT/DATA next for that endpoint). After OUT/DATA: device ACK -> room for another wMaxPacketSize, host continues OUT/DATA directly; device NYET -> accepted this payload but no room for next, host must return to PING probing. This 4-state ACK/NAK/NYET/PING handshake is the literal FSM a bulk/control-OUT endpoint model or scoreboard must implement. TRANSFER TYPES (ch.5, p.36-53, lines 2837-3806): four types with distinct semantic contracts. CONTROL (5.5, 2924-3136): Setup+Data(0+)+Status transaction sequence; bidirectional message pipe sharing one endpoint number; max payload FS={8,16,32,64}B selectable, HS fixed 64B, LS fixed 8B; data-stage completes on exact expected count OR short/zero-length packet; bus reservation >=10% frame (FS/LS) / >=20% microframe (HS); ceilings <29 FS 8B transfers/frame, <4 LS 8B/frame, <32 HS 64B/microframe. ISOCHRONOUS (5.6, 3208-3401): guaranteed bandwidth+bounded latency+constant rate but explicitly NO RETRY on error and NO HALT capability at all (no handshake mechanism exists for this type -- 'the low-level USB protocol does not allow handshakes to be returned to the transmitter of an isochronous pipe', line 3384-97); uni-directional stream pipe; max payload FS=1023B, HS=1024B (high-bandwidth HS endpoints get 2-3 transactions/microframe); period = 2^(bInterval-1) x F, bInterval 1-16, F=125us(HS)/1ms(FS); default interface settings must NOT include non-zero-payload isochronous endpoints; periodic (iso+interrupt) frame allocation ceiling <=90% FS frame / <=80% HS microframe. INTERRUPT (5.7, 3402-3427+): guaranteed max service period WITH retry on occasional error (unlike isochronous); uni-directional; max payload FS<=64B, HS<=1024B (high-bandwidth variant same as iso). BULK (5.8, 3630-3806): bandwidth-available, retryable, guaranteed delivery but no bandwidth/latency guarantee; uni-directional; max payload FS={8,16,32,64}B, HS fixed 512B; LOW-SPEED DEVICES MUST NOT HAVE BULK ENDPOINTS AT ALL (line 3658-60); completion rule same shape as control (exact count or short/zero packet); control transfers have bus priority over bulk; HS bulk-OUT must support PING; ceilings <72 FS 8B/frame, <14 HS 512B/microframe. Worked numeric bandwidth tables exist for all four types (Tables 5-1/5-2 control, 5-4/5-5 isochronous, 5-9/5-10 bulk) with real B/s and %-frame-bandwidth figures per payload size -- see full report for the transcribed table values. DESCRIPTORS (ch.9.6, p.261-271, lines 14190-14837): Device descriptor (Table 9-8, 18 bytes) -- bMaxPacketSize0 valid only in {8,16,32,64} and MUST be 64 at HS; bNumConfigurations counts only the current-speed config set, not both speeds. Device_Qualifier (Table 9-9, 10 bytes) -- describes the device's OTHER-speed characteristics; a FS-only device receiving this request must respond with a request error. Configuration descriptor (Table 9-10, 9 bytes) -- wTotalLength covers the ENTIRE returned tree (config+interface+endpoint+class descriptors), not just the 9-byte header; bmAttributes D6=self-powered,D5=remote-wakeup. Other_Speed_Configuration -- structurally identical to Configuration, host must retrieve device_qualifier successfully BEFORE requesting this (ordering dependency). Interface descriptor (Table 9-12, 9 bytes) -- bNumEndpoints always EXCLUDES endpoint 0; each alternate setting gets its own full interface+endpoint descriptor block, only bAlternateSetting changes across alternates of the same bInterfaceNumber. Endpoint descriptor (Table 9-13, 7 bytes) -- bmAttributes bits1:0 Transfer Type encoding 00=Control/01=Isochronous/10=Bulk/11=Interrupt (the literal encoding a descriptor-parsing monitor decodes); for isochronous only, bits3:2=Sync Type, bits5:4=Usage Type; wMaxPacketSize bits12:11 (HS iso/interrupt only) encode additional transactions per microframe (00=1 total,01=2,10=3,11=reserved); bInterval has FOUR DIFFERENT semantic meanings depending on transfer-type+speed+direction (iso/HS-interrupt=exponent period 2^(bInterval-1); FS/LS-interrupt=literal 1-255; HS bulk/control-OUT=max NAK rate encoding, 0=never NAKs) -- a common source of generator/model bugs if bInterval is treated as one uniform field.
